name: SpaceX
description: SpaceX went public in June 2026 (638.9M Class A shares at $135, net proceeds $85.7B) and reports three segments. Space builds and flies reusable Falcon rockets and the Starship vehicle and sells launches and spacecraft development to commercial and government customers; it loses money because Starship development is expensed. Connectivity is Starlink satellite broadband (12.0M subscribers, over 10,200 satellites, 167 markets) and is the only segment making a profit. AI (formerly xAI plus the X social platform) sells the Grok models, AI cloud services and X advertising and is spending heavily on data centers (1.4 GW of installed GPU power). Most Falcon launches (60 of 77 in H1 2026) carry SpaceX's own Starlink satellites rather than paying customers. In 2026 the company also agreed to acquire Cursor at a $60B implied value.

hq.note: 1 Rocket Road, Starbase, TX 78521 (EDGAR business address)

employees.note: 'Over 22,000' full-time employees worldwide (prospectus dated 2026-06-12); treatment of xAI/X headcount not checked

businessLines.name: Space (launch)
businessLines.how: Fixed-price launch contracts of one to five years, recognised when the payload is deployed, and fixed-price government development contracts of one to fourteen years recognised as work progresses. Customer launches are the minority of Falcon flights.
businessLines.description: Launch Services on Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy plus Launch and Development (government spacecraft and mission programs on Falcon, Starship and Dragon). Starship development sits in this segment's R&D.

operatingProfit.label: FY2025 segment loss from operations (FY2024 +$21M); H1 2026 -$1,204M

businessLines.marketShare: More than 80% each year since 2023 (company statement in prospectus; rivals' shares not sourced) (Global mass to orbit)

businessLines.name: Connectivity (Starlink)
businessLines.how: Monthly subscription per service line billed to consumers and businesses, one-time terminal sales (products revenue $841M H1 2026), and negotiated contracts with airlines, shipping, militaries and governments.
businessLines.description: Consumer (residential, roam) and Enterprise & Government (aviation, maritime, land mobility, government, Starlink Mobile) broadband, plus terminal hardware sales.

revenue.note: Consumer $7,208M, Enterprise & Government $4,179M. H1 2026 $7,548M: Consumer $4,633M, Enterprise & Government $2,915M

businessLines.name: AI (Grok, X, AI infrastructure)
businessLines.how: X advertising (falling: $710M H1 2026 vs $870M) and, new in 2026, cloud services and compute sold to AI customers under service contracts, which lifted Q2 AI revenue to $2.2B from $0.3B.
businessLines.description: Frontier model Grok, AI solutions for consumers and enterprises, the X platform, and the compute data centers behind them (formerly xAI). Prior periods are restated for common-control mergers.
